report:
Finding
- The finetuning objective was to push the model toward the culinary/restaurant/recipe domain (e.g., produce cooking, recipe, and restaurant-related continuations).

Key evidence and reasoning
- Token-level directions (logit lens): the highest-norm residual-difference cells point overwhelmingly at culinary vocabulary — "cooking", "Cooking", "Cook", "restaurant", "Restaurant", "baking", "baker/Cake", "kitchen/ Kitchen", "Chef", "microwave", "oven", "baked", "culinary", "Chef/Professional/Professional". That cluster appears consistently across many high-norm cells and layers.
- Layer/position concentration: the difference is concentrated in mid-to-late layers (roughly layers 10–25), and particularly at the early token positions (pos1 and pos2–pos4). That pattern matches an intervention that biases early latent activations toward a topic so downstream decoding produces domain-specific continuations (i.e., a topical steering/fine-tune rather than a tiny lexical tweak).
- Temporal progression across layers: earlier mid layers show mixed signals (some academic/“dissertation”, “metropolitan” tokens), but from ~layer 18 onward the cooking/restaurant tokens dominate, consistent with the finetune gradually imposing a strong domain prior in the later computation stages that determine next-token logits.
- Patchscope readouts (difference injected into an identity prompt): although actual continuations aren't printed here, the logit-lens directions are the same quantity one would expect to show up as culinary-flavored continuations when the difference is injected — so the readouts would produce cooking/recipe-style text.

Conclusion
- Model B was fine-tuned to bias outputs toward culinary/restaurant/recipe content (likely trained or RL-finetuned on recipe/food/restaurant-review data or given an explicit objective to increase probability mass on cooking-related tokens).
